name: Marcus

income.note: Effective tax rate ~22% including federal + OH state income tax (3.99%)

monthly_surplus_note: Extremely tight. Marcus's $72K salary looks adequate on paper but a used car payment + healthcare + rent leaves very little room. Reflects research: average ops manager in mid-cost city runs near break-even after fixed costs.

savings_breakdown.note: 401K is the primary wealth-building vehicle. Liquid savings cover less than 1 month of expenses — below Bankrate's 3-month recommendation. Empower data: median 401K for 30s cohort is $80K on avg income of $89K. Marcus is below median for his cohort, partially because he started contributing late (age 29).

debt_breakdown.auto_loan_note: Used 2022 Honda CR-V. National avg auto loan balance $24,297 (Experian 2024). Marcus is below average — bought used. Monthly payment $525 vs national avg $525 for used cars.
debt_breakdown.credit_card_note: Near Millennial avg of $6,961 (Experian 2025). Carries balance at 20.5% APR. Uses rewards card but rarely pays full balance.
debt_breakdown.bnpl_note: Has 3 active BNPL plans (Affirm x2, Klarna x1) from electronics and furniture purchases. This is off-balance-sheet debt — a common blind spot for comparison shoppers who use BNPL to 'optimize' large purchases.

financial_goals: Pay off auto loan 18 months early
Build liquid emergency fund to 3 months ($13,200)
subscriptions_detail: LinkedIn Premium ($39.99 — for job market awareness)

behavioral_profile.money_script: If I research long enough, I'll find the objectively right purchase — and then I deserve it.
spending_triggers: Finding a 'deal' after extended research (justifies purchase as rational)
BNPL availability — removes sticker shock, enables larger purchases
Work stress paired with a productivity-framed purchase ('I need this for work')
Competitive benchmarking — peers at work buying similar items
cognitive_biases_observed: Anchoring: anchors to MSRP then feels any discount justifies buying
The research justification trap: long research process creates sunk cost, making purchase feel inevitable
BNPL blind spot: treats installment payments as 'not real debt' — has $4K off-balance-sheet
Optimism bias: consistently underestimates how long debt repayment takes
shopping_patterns: Reads 50+ reviews on Amazon, Reddit r/BuyItForLife, YouTube review channels
2 in 3 shoppers actively hunt for discounts before purchasing (TGM Research 2024 — Marcus is this shopper)
1 in 4 shoppers conduct specific product research before buying (Marcus is strongly in this group)
Uses BNPL for purchases over $300 — considers it 'smart cash flow management'
Shops primarily on Amazon, Best Buy, and Wirecutter-recommended retailers
behavioral_profile.financial_anxiety_notes: Marcus is aware his budget is tight but frames it as temporary. He experiences anxiety around retirement adequacy — his 401K is behind for his age cohort. Men in their 30s are 30% higher spending on transportation (FinanceBuzz 2024) — the car payment reflects this pattern.
behavioral_profile.decision_making_note: Ops manager mindset carries into personal finance — seeks to optimize, compare, and systematize. Research process can become a justification ritual rather than a genuine decision filter.

demo_context.coaching_note: At $277/month surplus with $4K BNPL already outstanding, a $1,200 purchase triggers Deal Hunter. Marcus will rationalize it as a 'work necessity' — coach should name that pattern.

data_sources: Experian – Average Auto Loan Debt Study 2024
Experian – Average Credit Card Debt by Age 2025
Motley Fool – 2025 Buy Now Pay Later Trends Study
FinanceBuzz – Male vs Female Spending Statistics
